paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 3a. “אמרו לפניו רבונו של עולם, תנה לנו מראש ונעשנה. אמר להן הקב״ה: שוטים שבעולם, מי שטרח בערב שבת יאכל בשבת, מי שלא טרח בערב שבת מהיכן יאכל בשבת? אלא אף על פי כן, מצוה קלה יש לי וסוכה שמה, לכו ועשו אותה. מיד כל אחד ואחד נוטל והולך ועושה סוכה בראש גגו, והקב״ה מקדיר עליהם חמה בתקופת תמוז, וכל אחד ואחד מבעט בסוכתו ויוצא.” The nations said to Him, “Master of the world, give us the Torah from the beginning and we will observe it.” The Holy One, blessed be He, answered them, “Fools of the world. Whoever toiled on the eve of Shabbos will eat on Shabbos. Whoever did not toil on the eve of Shabbos, from where will he eat on Shabbos? Even so, I have an easy commandment called sukkah. Go and do it.” Immediately each went and built a sukkah on his roof. The Holy One, blessed be He, made the sun beat down on them at its summer strength. Each kicked his sukkah and left.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 3:1–5. “והנחש היה ערום מכל חית השדה אשר עשה ה׳ אלהים. ויאמר אל האשה: אף כי אמר אלהים לא תאכלו מכל עץ הגן. ותאמר האשה אל הנחש: מפרי עץ הגן נאכל. ומפרי העץ אשר בתוך הגן אמר אלהים: לא תאכלו ממנו ולא תגעו בו פן תמתון. ויאמר הנחש אל האשה: לא מות תמתון, כי ידע אלהים כי ביום אכלכם ממנו ונפקחו עיניכם, והייתם כאלהים ידעי טוב ורע.” The serpent was more crafty than any wild animal Hashem God had made. He said to the woman, “Did God really say that you may not eat of any tree of the garden?” The woman replied to the serpent, “We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden. Of the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, God said that we must not eat of it or touch it, lest we die.” The serpent told the woman, “You will not die. God knows that on the day you eat of it, your eyes will open and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”

paragraphs.text: Avos and Pesachim 1:3 and 50b. “אנטיגנוס איש סוכו קבל משמעון הצדיק, הוא היה אומר: אל תהיו כעבדים המשמשין את הרב על מנת לקבל פרס, אלא הוו כעבדים המשמשין את הרב שלא על מנת לקבל פרס. ויהי מורא שמים עליכם. אמר רב יהודה אמר רב: לעולם יעסוק אדם בתורה ובמצות אף על פי שלא לשמה, שמתוך שלא לשמה בא לשמה.” Antigonus of Socho received the tradition from Shimon the Righteous. He used to say, “Do not be like servants serving their master in order to receive a reward. Be like servants who serve their master without aiming to receive a reward, and let fear of Heaven be upon you.” Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav, “A person should always engage in Torah and mitzvos even with a motive other than their own sake, for from doing them with such a motive he comes to do them for their own sake.”

paragraphs.text: Devarim 25:17–19. “זכור את אשר עשה לך עמלק בדרך בצאתכם ממצרים, אשר קרך בדרך ויזנב בך כל הנחשלים אחריך ואתה עיף ויגע, ולא ירא אלהים. והיה בהניח ה׳ אלהיך לך מכל איביך מסביב בארץ אשר ה׳ אלהיך נתן לך נחלה לרשתה תמחה את זכר עמלק מתחת השמים, לא תשכח.” Remember what Amalek did to you on the way as you left Egypt. He met you on the road and attacked all the stragglers at your rear when you were faint and weary. He did not fear God. When Hashem your God gives you rest from all your enemies around you, in the land Hashem your God gives you to inherit, you shall erase the memory of Amalek from beneath the heavens. Do not forget.

paragraphs.text: Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 3:8. “והיה כאשר ירים משה ידו וגבר ישראל וגומר. וכי ידיו של משה עושות מלחמה או שוברות מלחמה? אלא לומר לך: כל זמן שהיו ישראל מסתכלים כלפי מעלה ומשעבדין את לבם לאביהם שבשמים היו מתגברים, ואם לאו היו נופלין.” “When Moshe raised his hand, Israel prevailed,” and so on. Could Moshe’s hands wage a war or defeat one? The verse teaches that whenever Israel looked upward and subjected their hearts to their Father in Heaven, they prevailed. Otherwise they fell.

paragraphs.text: I Shmuel 15:7–9. “ויחמל שאול והעם על אגג ועל מיטב הצאן והבקר והמשנים ועל הכרים ועל כל הטוב ולא אבו החרימם.” Shaul struck down Amalek from Chavilah as far as Shur, which faces Egypt. He captured Agag, king of Amalek, alive, and put all the people under the ban by the sword. Shaul and the people spared Agag, the finest of the sheep and cattle, the fatlings, the lambs, and everything choice, and they refused to destroy them. All the property they regarded as worthless and inferior they destroyed.

paragraphs.text: Megillah 12b–13a. “ומה שילם לי ימיני דלא קטליה שאול לאגג דאיתיליד מיניה המן דמצער לישראל.” Rava said that Knesses Yisrael spoke of it in the opposite sense: “See what a Yehudite did to me, and what a Binyaminite repaid me.” What did the Yehudite do? David did not kill Shimi, from whom Mordechai descended, and Haman was provoked by Mordechai. What did the Binyaminite repay me? Shaul did not kill Agag, from whom Haman descended, and Haman brought trouble upon Israel.

paragraphs.text: Yoma 22b. “שאול באחת ועלתה לו דוד בשתים ולא עלתה לו.” Rav Huna said: How little a man whom his Master assists fears or feels the danger. Shaul erred once and lost the kingship. David erred twice and did not lose it. What was Shaul’s one error? The episode of Agag. But there was also the episode of Nov, the city of priests. It is of Agag that Scripture says, “I regret that I made Shaul king.” What were David’s two errors? The matter of Uriah and the incitement that led him to count Israel.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 107a. “אתא שטן אידמי ליה כציפרתא פתק ביה גירא פתקה לחלתא איגליה וחזייה.” “He walked on the roof of the royal house and saw a woman bathing from the roof. The woman was very beautiful.” Bathsheva was washing her head under a screen. Satan came in the form of a bird. David shot an arrow, which struck the screen and made it fall, and he saw her. At once “David sent to inquire about the woman.” He was told, “It is Bathsheva daughter of Eliam, wife of Uriah the Hittite.” David sent messengers, took her, and lay with her. She had cleansed herself of her impurity, and she returned home.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 93b. “וה׳ עמו שהלכה כמותו בכל מקום. ... בכולהו אמר להו יהונתן בני כמוהו כיון דאמר ליה וה׳ עמו מילתא דבדידיה נמי לא הוה חלש דעתיה ואיקניא ביה.” “One of the young men answered, ‘I have seen a son of Yishai of Beis Lechem, who knows how to play, is mighty and a man of war, discerning in speech and of appearance, and Hashem is with him.’” Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: Doeg said this entire verse as malicious speech. “Knows how to play” means that he knows how to ask. “Mighty” means that he knows how to answer. “A man of war” means that he knows how to debate in the battle of Torah. “Discerning in speech” means that he understands one thing from another. “Of appearance” means that he can show the faces of halachah. “Hashem is with him” means that the halachah follows him everywhere. To all the others Shaul said, “My son Yehonasan is his equal.” When Doeg said, “Hashem is with him,” a quality Shaul himself lacked, his resolve weakened, and he became jealous.

paragraphs.text: Yoma 82b–83a. “לחושו לה ולא אילחישא ... נפק מינה שבתאי אצר פירי.” A pregnant woman smelled food on Yom Kippur and craved it. They came before Rabbi. He told them to whisper to her that it was Yom Kippur. They did so, and her craving subsided. He applied to her the verse, “Before I formed you in the womb I knew you,” and Rabbi Yochanan was born to her. Another pregnant woman smelled food. They came before Rabbi Chanina. He said, “Whisper to her,” but her craving did not subside and they had to feed her. He applied to her the verse, “The wicked go astray from the womb,” and she bore Shabsai the hoarder of produce, who was wicked.

paragraphs.text: Ta’anis 23b. “עשה בשביל אלו שאין מכירין בין אבא דיהיב מיטרא לאבא דלא יהיב מיטרא.” Chanan the Hidden was a grandson of Choni HaMe’aggel through his daughter. When the world needed rain, the sages sent schoolchildren to him. They held the hems of his garment and said, “Father, Father, give us rain.” He said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, do this for those who cannot distinguish the Father who gives rain from the father who cannot.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 102a. “בעת רצון עניתיך ... עת מזומנת לטובה. וביום פקדי ופקדתי עלהם חטאתם ... עת היא מזומנת לפורענות.” “In a time of favor I answered you.” A baraisa in Rabbi Yose’s name teaches that there is a time appointed for good. “On the day I take account, I will take account of their sin.” A baraisa in Rabbi Yose’s name teaches that there is a time appointed for calamity. “Rechavam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.” A baraisa in Rabbi Yose’s name teaches that it is a place appointed for calamity. At Shechem they violated Dinah, at Shechem the brothers sold Yosef, and at Shechem the kingdom of the house of David was divided.

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 10b–11a. “בניסן נגאלו בתשרי עתידין ליגאל. רבי יהושע אומר ... בניסן נגאלו בניסן עתידין ליגאל.” Rabbi Eliezer says that the world was created in Tishrei, the patriarchs were born in Tishrei, and the patriarchs died in Tishrei. Yitzchak was born on Pesach. Sarah, Rachel, and Channah were remembered on Rosh Hashanah. Yosef left prison on Rosh Hashanah, and the bondage of our ancestors in Egypt ceased on Rosh Hashanah. In Nissan they were redeemed and in Tishrei they will be redeemed. Rabbi Yehoshua says that the world was created in Nissan, the patriarchs were born in Nissan, and the patriarchs died in Nissan. Yitzchak was born on Pesach. Sarah, Rachel, and Channah were remembered on Rosh Hashanah. Yosef left prison on Rosh Hashanah, and the bondage of our ancestors in Egypt ceased on Rosh Hashanah. In Nissan they were redeemed and in Nissan they will be redeemed. Sanhedrin 97b records Rabbi Eliezer’s view that Israel will be redeemed if they repent. Rabbi Yehoshua asks whether they would then remain unredeemed if they did not repent. God will raise up a king whose decrees are as severe as Haman’s, bringing Israel to repentance and back to the good. Each goes on to cite verses for his position, and Rabbi Eliezer finally fell silent.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin and Rashi 106b. “איה ספר את המגדלים ... שהיה סופר שלש מאות הלכות פסוקות במגדל הפורח באויר.” Rabbi Yitzchak said: What is meant by “Where is the scribe? Where is the weigher? Where is the one who counts the towers?” “Where is the scribe?” refers to one who counted all the letters of Torah. “Where is the weigher?” refers to one who weighed the Torah’s cases of lesser and greater severity. “Where is the one who counts the towers?” refers to one who counted three hundred decided laws concerning the tower that flies in the air. Rashi explains this as asking why the upper stroke above the lamed curves downward. Chagigah 15b records Rabbi Ami’s statement that Doeg and Achitofel posed three hundred questions concerning the tower that flies in the air.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 107a. “בשעה שהן עוסקין בארבע מיתות בית דין פוסקין ממשנתן ואומרים לי דוד הבא על אשת איש מיתתו במה.” Rava expounded: What does it mean, “When I stumbled they rejoiced and gathered. Unworthy men gathered against me, and I did not know. They tore and did not cease”? David said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, You know that if they tore my flesh, my blood would not flow. Moreover, when they study the four court-administered deaths, they interrupt to ask me, “David, how is one who lies with a married woman put to death?” I answered them that one who lies with a married woman is put to death by strangulation and has a share in the World to Come. One who shames another publicly has no share in the World to Come.

Unworthy men gathered against me, and I did not know. They tore and did not cease”? David said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, You know that if they tore my flesh, my blood would not flow. Moreover, when they study the four court-administered deaths, they interrupt to ask me, “David, how is one who lies with a married woman put to death?” I answered them that one who lies with a married woman is put to death by strangulation and has a share in the World to Come. One who shames another publicly has no share in the World to Come.

paragraphs.text: Niddah 8b. “שלוש בתולות הן בתולת אדם בתולת קרקע בתולת שקמה.” Rav Kahana said: A baraisa teaches three kinds of virginity, in a person, land, and a sycamore. A person is a virgin as long as she has not had relations. This matters for marriage to a high priest or for a kesubah of two hundred. Virgin land is land that has never been worked. This matters for the valley of the broken-necked heifer or for sale and purchase. A virgin sycamore is one that has never been cut. This matters for sale and purchase or for cutting it in the Sabbatical year.

paragraphs.text: Eruvin 54b. “מה תאנה זו כל זמן שאדם ממשמש בה מוצא בה תאנים אף דברי תורה כל זמן שאדם הוגה בהן מוצא בהן טעם.” Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: What is meant by “He who tends a fig tree will eat its fruit”? Why is Torah compared to a fig tree? As often as a person handles a fig tree he finds figs on it, and as often as one studies Torah he finds meaning in it. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani asked the meaning of “A beloved hind and a graceful doe,” and why Torah is likened to a hind. The hind is physically narrow and dear to its mate at every moment as in the first moment. Torah too is dear to those who study it at every moment as in the first moment.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 72:5. “וכל השבח הזה מנין היה לו ליששכר? משל זבולן, שהיה עוסק בפדגמטיא שלו ומאכיל את יששכר שהיה בן תורה” Yissachar was ninth among the tribes and made his offering second to the king, as it says, “On the second day Nesanel ben Tzuar, the prince of Yissachar, made his offering.” Why? Because he was a man of Torah. … How did Yissachar come to deserve all this praise? Through Zevulun, who engaged in trade and supported Yissachar, a man of Torah. This is what it says, “Zevulun shall dwell by the seashore.” When Moshe came to bless the tribes, he placed Zevulun’s blessing before Yissachar’s: “Rejoice, Zevulun, in your going out, and Yissachar, in your tents.”

paragraphs.text: Shemos Rabbah 40:3. “עד שאדם הראשון מוטל גולם הראה לו הקדוש ברוך הוא כל צדיק וצדיק שעתיד לעמוד ממנו” What is the meaning of “It was known that he is adam”? While Adam was still an unformed body, the Holy One, blessed be He, showed him every righteous person who was to descend from him. One was associated with Adam’s head, another with his hair, another with his forehead, and others with his eyes, nose, mouth, ear, or the place of the nose ring. Consider this: When Iyov wanted to dispute with the Holy One and said, “If only I knew where to find Him, I would lay out my case before Him,” the Holy One answered, “You want to dispute with Me? Where were you when I founded the earth?” What is the meaning of eifo, “where”? Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said that the Holy One told Iyov, “Tell Me where your portion was attached. Was it in his head, his forehead, or some other limb? If you know where your portion was, then you may dispute with Me.”

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tehillim 1:4. “אשריהם הנביאים שהן מדמין את הצורה ליוצרה ואת הנטיעה לנוטעה.” Chizkiyah bar Chiya said: Fortunate are the prophets, who liken the form to the One who made it, and the planting to the One who planted it. Thus it says, “For Hashem God is a sun and a shield,” and “A lion roars, who will not fear?” It also says, “The glory of the God of Israel came from the east, His voice like the sound of many waters, and the earth shone with His glory.” The ear is made to hear what it can hear, and the eye is made to see what it can see.

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 56a. “אמרו לו בניו שמע ישראל ה׳ אלהינו ה׳ אחד אמרו כשם שאין בלבך אלא אחד כך אין בלבנו אלא אחד.” Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish taught: “Yaakov called to his sons and said, ‘Gather and I will tell you.’” Yaakov wished to disclose the final end to his sons, but the Shechinah withdrew from him. He said, “Could there be, Heaven forbid, a disqualified child among my children, as Yishmael came from Avraham and Esav came from my father Yitzchak?” His sons replied, “Hear, Israel, Hashem is our God, Hashem is one. Just as there is only One in your heart, there is only One in ours.” Then Yaakov said, “Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.” The sages asked what they should do. Moshe did not say it, so how could they say it? Yaakov said it, so how could they omit it? They instituted saying it quietly. Rabbi Yitzchak quoted the school of Rabbi Ami: It is like a princess who smelled the cooked food sticking to a pot. To ask for it would embarrass her, and to refrain would pain her. Her servants began to bring it quietly. Rabbi Abahu said that they instituted saying it aloud because of the objections of the sectarians. In Neharde’a, where there were no sectarians, they still said it quietly.

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 18a. “בראש השנה כל באי העולם עוברין לפניו כבני מרון. ... אמר רבה בר בר חנה אמר רבי יוחנן וכולן נסקרין בסקירה אחת.” On Rosh Hashanah all who enter the world pass before Him like bnei maron. What does that mean? Here they rendered it as lambs. Rashi explains that sheep being counted for the tithe go through a narrow opening singly, since they cannot pass through together. Reish Lakish said it is like the ascent of Beis Maron. Rav Yehudah said in Shmuel’s name that it means like the troops of the house of David. Rabbah bar bar Chanah said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name that they are all surveyed in a single glance.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 6a. “אינהו נפישי מינן וקיימי עלן כי כסלא לאוגיא.” A baraisa teaches in Abba Binyamin’s name that if the eye were granted permission to see, no creature could withstand the damaging spirits. Abaye said they are more numerous than we are and stand around us like a ridge around a furrow. Rashi describes a ring of dug earth encircling a hollow made beneath grapevines.

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 16a. “אמרו לפני בראש השנה מלכיות זכרונות ושופרות, מלכיות כדי שתמליכוני עליכם, זכרונות כדי שיעלה זכרוניכם לפני לטובה, ובמה בשופר.” The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Pour water before Me on the festival, so that the year’s rains will be blessed for you. Recite before Me on Rosh Hashanah the verses of Kingship, Remembrance, and Shofar. Recite Kingship to make Me King over you, and Remembrance so that your memory will come before Me for good. By what means? By the shofar. Rabbi Abahu asked why we sound a ram’s horn. The Holy One said to sound a ram’s horn before Him so that He will remember the binding of Yitzchak son of Avraham, and He will count it as though we had bound ourselves before Him.

paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 76a–b. “אף מי שהיה מוכתב באסטרטיא של מלך ... בחיילות של בית דוד.” In the Mishnah Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says that a woman may marry into the priesthood based on an ancestor having been registered in the king’s army, without a further lineage check. The Gemara on the next side quotes Rav Yehudah in Shmuel’s name: This refers to the troops of the house of David. Rav Yosef asks for the verse and cites, “They were registered by lineage in the army for war.” Rav Yehudah says in Rav’s name that this was so their own merit and their ancestors’ merit would assist them.

paragraphs.text: Mishlei and Sotah 6:23 and 21a. “כי נר מצוה ותורה אור ודרך חיים תוכחות מוסר. ... מה נר אינה מגינה אלא לפי שעה אף מצוה אינה מגינה אלא לפי שעה, ואת התורה באור לומר לך מה אור מגין לעולם אף תורה מגינה לעולם.” “For a mitzvah is a lamp and Torah is light, and the rebukes of discipline are a way of life.” Rabbi Menachem bar Yose expounded in Sotah 21a that Scripture likens the mitzvah to a lamp and Torah to light. A lamp protects only for a time, and a mitzvah protects only for a time. Light protects perpetually, and Torah protects perpetually. “When you walk, it will guide you” refers to this world, “when you lie down, it will guard you” to death, and “when you awaken, it will speak with you” to the future. It is like a man walking at dead of night, afraid of thorns, pits, and briars, wild animals, and robbers, without knowing whether he is on the right road. When he found a torch, he was saved from the thorns, pits, and briars. He still feared wild animals and robbers, and did not know his way. When dawn broke, he was saved from wild animals and robbers, but still did not know his way. When he reached the crossroads, he was saved from them all.

paragraphs.text: Nedarim 31a. “שאיני נהנה לזרע אברהם אסור בישראל ומותר בעובדי כוכבים ... והאיכא עשו? ביצחק, ולא כל יצחק.” The Mishnah rules that one who vows not to benefit from Avraham’s offspring is forbidden to benefit from Israel and permitted to benefit from the other nations. The Gemara asks about Yishmael and answers that Scripture says, “Through Yitzchak shall offspring be called yours.” It asks about Esav and answers that “through Yitzchak” means through some of his descendants.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis 30:37–39 and Rashi. “ויקח לו יעקב מקל לבנה לח ולוז וערמון” Yaakov took fresh rods of poplar, almond, and plane tree. He peeled white strips in them, exposing the white on the rods. He placed the rods he had peeled in the channels at the watering troughs where the flock came to drink, opposite the flock, so that they would come into heat when they came to drink. The flock came into heat at the rods and bore streaked, spotted, and speckled young. Rashi explains “strips” as successive peelings that made the rods mottled. On “they would come into heat” he explains that the female saw the rods and recoiled, the male mounted her, and she gave birth to young like them.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 8:5. “חסד ואמת נפגשו צדק ושלום נשקו ... אמת מארץ תצמח” Rabbi Simon said that when the Holy One, blessed be He, came to create the first human, the ministering angels formed groups and companies. Some said that the human should be created, and some said he should not. This is the meaning of “Kindness and truth meet, righteousness and peace kiss.” Kindness said to create him because he would do acts of kindness. Truth said to refrain, because he would be full of lies. Righteousness said to create him because he would perform charitable deeds. Peace said to refrain, because he would be full of strife. What did the Holy One do? He took truth and cast it to earth, as it says, “You cast truth to earth.” The ministering angels said before Him, “Master of the worlds, why do You dishonor the emblem that is Yours? Let truth rise from the earth.” Thus it says, “Truth will spring from the earth.”

paragraphs.text: Tanna Devei Eliyahu Zuta and Shelah §2 and Shaar HaOsiyos, Emes VeEmunah, Principle 8. “אחות לוטן תמנע ... ודבורי ה׳ ומאמריו הם כל פסוקיה ודבריה” Hence the sages said that even if a person knows neither Scripture nor Mishnah and spends the entire day reading “Lotan’s sister was Timna,” he earns the reward of Torah. The Shelah explains that Moshe our teacher wrote and inscribed as a scribe from the mouth of Hashem, from “In the beginning” all the way to “before the eyes of all Israel.” Moshe wrote the whole Torah from the mouth of the Holy One. There is no difference between “I am Hashem your God” and “Timna was a concubine,” or any verse like it. All is equal. Every verse and every word is the speech and utterance of Hashem.

paragraphs.text: Tanchuma Ki Seitzei §7. “לזה הזכרתי על קערה מלא כל טוב ולזה הזכרתי על קערה ריקם” To what may this be compared? To a king who held a feast and invited guests. A bowl filled with every good thing was brought before him. He said, “Remember so-and-so who loves me.” When the bowl had been cleared, he said, “Remember so-and-so who hates me.” His friends said, “You mentioned this one and you mentioned that one.” He told them, “I remembered this one over a bowl full of good things and that one over an empty bowl.” So of Shabbos it is written, “Remember the day of Shabbos to sanctify it,” and one honors it with food, drink, and clean clothing. Of Amalek it is written, “Remember what Amalek did to you.” Over what should you remember it? Over an empty table, as it says, “You shall blot out the memory of Amalek from under the heavens.”

paragraphs.text: Ramban to Deuteronomy 25:17 distinguishes remembering Amalek aloud from retaining the memory in the heart. He considers the public reading of Parashat Zachor as a form of spoken remembrance and emphasizes telling later generations what Amalek did. His distinction gives context to Rav Tzadok’s movement from public reading to a remembrance fixed in the heart.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 156a and Tosafos. “מזל מחכים מזל מעשיר ויש מזל לישראל ... אין מזל לישראל” Rabbi Chanina says mazal makes one wise and wealthy, and Israel is subject to mazal. Rabbi Yochanan says Israel is not subject to mazal. He derives it from “Do not learn the way of the nations and do not be dismayed at the signs of the heavens, though the nations are dismayed at them.” The nations fear them, whereas Israel does not. Rav also holds that Israel is not subject to mazal, deriving it from “He took him outside.” Avraham told the Holy One that a member of his household would inherit him. Hashem replied that his own offspring would inherit him. Avraham said that by his astrology he was unfit to father a son. He was told to go outside his astrology, since Israel is not subject to mazal. If his reason was that Jupiter was in the west, Hashem would move it to the east. Tosafos address the statement of Rava at the end of Moed Katan that children, life, and sustenance depend on mazal. They explain that great merit can change it, yet at times it does not change, as Yevamos 50a says, “If he merits, they add to his years. If he does not, they reduce them.”

Rav Tzadok uses Rashi’s gloss to identify the mazal as an advocate above.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 32a. “אם יש עליו מלאך מליץ אחד מני אלף” Repentance and good deeds are a person’s advocates. Even if nine hundred and ninety-nine plead for conviction and only one pleads for merit, he is saved. As it says, “If there is for him an angel, an advocate, one among a thousand, to declare a man’s uprightness, He will be gracious to him and say, ‘Redeem him from descending to the pit,’” and so forth.

paragraphs.text: Pri Tzaddik, Vayera 4:1 “A person has a mazal. Rashi explains that this is his own angel, who intercedes for him. This corresponds to the levels of nefesh, ruach, and neshamah. Nefesh is from the world of action, ruach from the world of formation, the world of angels, and neshamah from the world of creation. Thus every person has his own angel in heaven by virtue of the level of ruach.” Rav Tzadok applies this account to Avraham’s three visitors and to the distinct roles of the patriarchs. The parallel shows how a particular angelic power can correspond to the character of an individual soul.

paragraphs.text: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 16:19 “Whatever concerns Torah and mitzvot certainly depends on merit, because the reward for a mitzvah is a mitzvah. One who comes to purify himself receives all kinds of help, including the children, life, and sustenance he needs to serve God, and all the more so children through whom to fulfill the commandment to be fruitful and multiply. What depends on mazal and is decreed at formation includes what does not assist in serving God.” Likkutei Maamarim distinguishes the material help needed to fulfill a mitzvah from the broader conditions of life governed by mazal. It gives a practical application of the distinction developed here between merit and the soul’s allotted circumstances.

paragraphs.text: Tzidkas HaTzadik §169 “When a person is overtaken by fear of something, he should immediately ask for mercy to be spared from it. Heaven awakened this fear for that purpose, as our sages said, “A person should always pray before trouble comes.” … Through prayer he sweetens the decree at its root, so that what later comes forth is good.” Rav Tzadok applies the same principle to an unsettling foreboding. It can prompt prayer while there is still an opportunity to change a harsh decree at its source.

paragraphs.text: Koheles Rabbah 1:1. “אלא אני שואל בתו והכל ינתן לי בכלל בתו” Rabbi Simon said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta that a courtier grew up in a royal palace. The king invited him to ask what he should give him. The courtier reasoned that if he asked for silver, gold, beautiful jewels, or clothes, the king would give him those things. He would instead ask for the king’s daughter and receive everything along with her. So Hashem appeared to Shlomo at Givon in a dream and invited him to ask for a gift. Shlomo reasoned that if he asked for wealth he would receive it, but he would ask for wisdom and so obtain everything. This is the meaning of “Give Your servant a listening heart.” Since he asked for wisdom and did not ask for wealth, honor, or the lives of his enemies, the Holy One gave him wisdom and knowledge together with wealth, possessions, and honor.

paragraphs.text: Pirkei Avos 5:19. “עין טובה ורוח נמוכה ונפש שפלה ... עין רעה ורוח גבוהה ונפש רחבה” Whoever has the following three traits is among the disciples of Avraham our father, and one who has the opposite traits is among the disciples of the wicked Bilaam. A generous eye, a humble spirit, and a modest appetite mark Avraham’s disciples. A begrudging eye, a haughty spirit, and a large appetite mark Bilaam’s. Avraham’s disciples eat in this world and inherit in the World to Come, as it says, “I will give substance to those who love Me and fill their storehouses.” Bilaam’s disciples inherit Gehinnom and go down to the pit, as it says, “You, God, will bring them down to the pit of destruction. Men of blood and deceit will not live out half their days, but I trust in You.”

paragraphs.text: Takanas HaShavin 6:61 “Abraham fathered Isaac. Isaac, who is called his offspring and in whom the depths of Abraham’s heart were revealed, had a disposition of restraint and awe for the sake of Heaven. Through him it became clear that the kindness manifest in Abraham’s own disposition was likewise entirely for the sake of Heaven.” This gives an example of the tradition Rav Tzadok invokes here. A child can reveal a parent’s deepest intention through an outward disposition very different from the parent’s own.

paragraphs.text: Tzidkas HaTzadik §131 “Balaam knew that actions could change even the root. He did not tell them this, but spoke smoothly so that they would feel secure, sin, and alter the root. … God reversed it, making it truly so that even if they sinned, the root would remain unchanged. That is why his words were set down as Torah, for they are indeed true.” Rav Tzadok uses this distinction to explain why Balaam’s blessing became part of Torah. Balaam meant to invite complacency, yet the blessing ended up declaring the enduring bond from which he himself was excluded.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 12b. “בקשו לקבוע פרשת בלק בקריאת שמע ... משום טורח ציבור” Rabbi Abahu ben Zutarti said in the name of Rabbi Yehudah bar Zevida that they wanted to include the passage of Balak in Shema, but did not fix it there because it would burden the congregation. The Gemara asks whether it was for “God took them out of Egypt,” since then the sections on interest and weights, which also mention the Exodus, would serve as well. Rabbi Yose bar Avin says it was for “He crouched and lay down like a lion, like a lioness, who shall rouse him?” The Gemara asks why they could not recite that verse alone. We have a tradition that we may divide a passage only where Moshe our teacher divided it.

paragraphs.text: Menachos 29b. “שתוק כך עלה במחשבה לפני” Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav that when Moshe went up on high, he found the Holy One sitting and tying crowns onto the letters. He asked, “Master of the world, who is holding You back?” He told him that a man named Akiva ben Yosef would come after many generations and expound heaps of laws on every point. Moshe asked to see him, and Hashem told him to turn around. He went and sat at the end of eight rows. He did not know what they were saying and grew faint. When Rabbi Akiva came to one matter, the students asked how he knew it. He said that it was a law given to Moshe at Sinai, and Moshe was reassured. Moshe returned and asked the Holy One, “You have such a man and You are giving the Torah through me?” He answered, “Be silent. Thus it arose in thought before Me.” Moshe asked to see Rabbi Akiva’s reward after seeing his Torah. Hashem told him to turn around. He saw Rabbi Akiva’s flesh being weighed in the butcher stalls. He said, “Master of the world, this is Torah and this its reward?” He answered, “Be silent. Thus it arose in thought before Me.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar Bereishis 27a. “בחומר — בקל וחומר, ובלבנים — בלבון הלכתא” “They embittered their lives with hard labor” means through a difficult question. “With mortar” means by a kal vachomer. “With bricks” means through clarification of the halachah. “With all labor in the field” is baraisa, and “all their labor” is Mishnah.

paragraphs.text: Rashi to Rosh Hashanah 33b distinguishes the prolonged groans of a sick person from the short, consecutive cries of someone weeping. The uncertainty over which cry the Torah requires, or whether it requires both together, is reflected in the three patterns prescribed in Shulchan Arukh, Orach Chayim 590:2.

paragraphs.text: Shoftim 4:3, 7. “כי תשע מאות רכב ברזל לו ... ונתתיהו בידך” The children of Israel cried out to Hashem, for Sisera had nine hundred iron chariots and oppressed them with force for twenty years. Verse 7 states, “I will draw to you, to the Kishon, Sisera, the commander of Yavin’s army, and his chariots and his multitude, and I will give him into your hand.”

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tehillim 107:4. “כשם שהרועה נותן ידו ושומטה ממעיה ... ויוציא אתכם מכור הברזל ממצרים” Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said in the name of the sages, “Like a fetus inside an animal. As the shepherd reaches in and draws it from her womb, so the Holy One brought Israel out of Egypt,” as it says, “To go and take for Himself a nation from within a nation.” Rabbi Aivu said in the name of Rabbi Yose ben Zimra, “Just as a goldsmith stretches out his hand and takes gold from the furnace, so the Holy One brought Israel from Egypt’s hand,” as it says, “He brought you out of the iron furnace, from Egypt.”

paragraphs.text: Berachos 58a. “עביד רחמנא ניסא לשקרי הכי ... אשר בשר חמורים בשרם” Rabbi Sheila flogged a man who had relations with a gentile woman. The man denounced him to the government, alleging that a Jew was judging without royal authority. The court summoned Rabbi Sheila and asked why he had flogged the man. He answered that the man had relations with a donkey. They asked whether he had witnesses, and he said he did. Eliyahu appeared as a person and testified. They declared the man liable to death. Rabbi Sheila told them the Jews no longer had authority to execute since exile, and they could do as they saw fit. As he was leaving, the man asked, “Does the Merciful One perform such a miracle for falsehood?” Rabbi Sheila replied, “Wicked man, are they not called donkeys?” citing “whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys.” He saw the man was going to report that he had called them donkeys. Since this made him a pursuer and the Torah says to rise and kill one who comes to kill you, Rabbi Sheila struck him with a club and killed him.

paragraphs.text: Chagigah 2a. “כדרך שבא לראות כך בא ליראות” Yochanan ben Dehavai said in the name of Rabbi Yehudah that someone blind in one eye is exempt from appearing in the Temple. Scripture’s word is read both “he shall see” and “he shall appear.” Just as he comes to see, he comes to appear, and just as seeing is with two eyes, appearing calls for two eyes.

paragraphs.text: Ta’anis 25a. “מי שאמר לשמן וידלוק הוא יאמר לחומץ וידלוק” One Friday evening Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa saw that his daughter was sad. He asked her why. She told him that a vessel of vinegar had been confused with an oil vessel, and she had lit the Shabbos lamp from it. He told her that He who commanded oil to burn could command vinegar to burn. The lamp continued burning through the entire day and supplied a light for Havdalah.

paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 81a. “חזי דאת נורא ואנא בישרא ואנא עדיפנא מינך” Some redeemed captives came to Nehardea and were brought into the attic of Rav Amram Chasida’s house, and the ladder was removed. When one of them passed the opening, light fell through. Rav Amram took the ladder that ten people could not lift, and raised it alone. He started to climb. Halfway up he steadied himself and shouted that there was a fire at his house. The sages came and protested that he had put them to shame. He answered that it was better to be ashamed because of him in this world than in the next. He adjured the evil inclination to come out, and it emerged like a pillar of fire. He said to it, “See that you are fire and I am flesh, yet I am stronger than you.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Bereishis 17b, with HaSulam. There are two kinds of dispute, one at the beginning and one at the end. This is the way of the righteous: their beginning is difficult and their end peaceful. Korach represents the left at the beginning of the dispute between the right and the left. That dispute proceeds with anger and the force of stern judgments. Each side wishes to cancel the other’s illumination. Gehinnom issued from this, and Korach attached himself to Gehinnom. Shammai represents the left at the end of the dispute between right and left, once anger and wrath have subsided. At this stage one should awaken a dispute of love, in which each side illuminates in its own way. Through Heaven, the mediating line, the two sides gain agreement and endurance by being clothed in one another.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 11a. Rava bar Mechasya said in the name of Rav Chama bar Gurya in the name of Rav: If all the seas were ink, the reeds pens, the heavens sheets of writing material, and all people scribes, they would still be insufficient to record the breadth of the government’s concerns. Which verse teaches this? Rav Mesharshiya said, “The heavens for height, the earth for depth, and the heart of kings cannot be fathomed” (Mishlei 25:3).

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah and Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 3a and 4a. Each one of the nations immediately goes and builds a sukkah on his rooftop. The Holy One, blessed be He, causes the sun to beat down on them as in the summer season, and each one kicks his sukkah and leaves. As it is written, “Let us break their bonds and cast their cords away from us” (Tehillim 2:3). Rashi on Rosh Hashanah explains the distinction: an Israelite’s heart is directed to Heaven, and if his life takes an adverse turn, he does not complain but attributes his suffering to his sin. A non-Jew in the case discussed complains if he is not rewarded in kind.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 7b–8a. Rabbi Yitzchak said to Rav Nachman, “Why did the master not come to the synagogue to pray?” He replied, “I was unable to.” Rabbi Yitzchak said, “Let the master gather ten men and pray.” He replied, “That would be a burden for me.” Rabbi Yitzchak said, “Let the master ask the congregation’s representative to come and inform him when the congregation prays.” He replied, “Why go to such lengths?” Rabbi Yitzchak answered that Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: What does the verse “As for me, may my prayer be to You, Hashem, at a time of favor” (Tehillim 69:14) mean? When is a time of favor? When the congregation prays. Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Chanina derives it from “Thus says Hashem: In a time of favor I have answered you” (Yeshayahu 49:8).

paragraphs.text: Rabbeinu Yonah, Sha’arei Teshuvah II:1, lists six occasions that can awaken repentance, then urges daily repentance before any such occasion arrives. Keeping awareness of the Creator in mind can itself prompt return. This gives practical form to Rav Tzadok’s distinction between regular repentance and its heightened seasonal occasion.

paragraphs.text: Rif on Yoma 6a. Twenty-four things hinder teshuvah. These are tale-bearing and harmful speech, habitual anger, evil thoughts, associating with the wicked, becoming accustomed to meals whose hosts cannot afford them, looking at forbidden relations, sharing with a thief, saying “I will sin and repent,” gaining honor through another person’s disgrace, withdrawing from the community, disparaging one’s parents, disparaging one’s teachers, cursing the public, preventing the public from performing a mitzvah, leading another person from a good path to an evil path, using a poor person’s pledge, accepting a bribe to distort other people’s judgments, finding lost property and not returning it to its owner, seeing one’s son turn to evil ways and not objecting, consuming property robbed from the poor, orphans, and widows, disputing the words of the sages, suspecting the innocent, hating rebuke, and mocking the mitzvos.

paragraphs.text: Ta’anis and Rashi 5a. Rav Nachman said to Rabbi Yitzchak, “What does the verse ‘My people have committed two evils’ (Yirmiyahu 2:13) mean? Did they commit only two? Does it omit twenty-four?” He answered in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: It is one offense that is equal in gravity to two. Which one is it? Idolatry. For it says, “My people have committed two evils: they abandoned Me, the source of living water, to hew broken cisterns for themselves.” Rashi reads “Does it omit twenty-four?” as an astonished question. In the passage beginning “Will you judge?” in Yechezkel 22, there are twenty-four transgressions they committed. An alternate explanation is that they transgressed the twenty-four books of Scripture.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 6a and 7a. Rabbi Avin bar Rav Adda said in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak: From where do we know that the Holy One, blessed be He, lays tefillin? It is written, “Hashem has sworn by His right hand and by the arm of His might” (Yeshayahu 62:8). His right hand is Torah, as it says, “From His right hand came a fiery law for them” (Devarim 33:2). The arm of His might is tefillin, as it says, “Hashem gives might to His people” (Tehillim 29:11), and so forth. The two verses that begin “For what great nation,” which resemble one another, are in one compartment. “Fortunate are you, Israel” and “Who is like Your people Israel” are in one compartment. “Has God ever attempted” is in one compartment, and “To set you on high” is in one compartment. They are all written in His arm-tefillin. Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yosei: From where do we know that the Holy One, blessed be He, prays? It is written, “I shall bring them to My holy mountain and make them joyful in My house of prayer” (Yeshayahu 56:7). It says “My prayer,” not “their prayer.” From this we learn that the Holy One, blessed be He, prays. What does He pray? Rav Zutra bar Toviah said in the name of Rav: “May it be My will that My compassion overcome My anger, that My compassion prevail over My attributes, that I conduct Myself toward My children with compassion, and that I go beyond the strict measure of judgment on their behalf.”

paragraphs.text: Tosafos on Rosh Hashanah and Rashi on Bereishis 27a, s.v. k’man, and 1:1. Rabbi Eliezer HaKalir based the prayer for rain on Shemini Atzeres on Rabbi Eliezer, who holds that the world was created in Tishrei. In the Passover liturgy he followed Rabbi Yehoshua. Rabbeinu Tam says that these and those are the words of the living God. We can explain that in Tishrei the thought arose to create the world, but it was not created until Nisan. Rashi explains “God created” (Bereishis 1:1): It does not say “Hashem created,” because at first He intended to create it with the attribute of judgment. When He saw that the world could not endure, He gave precedence to compassion and joined it with judgment. This is why it says, “On the day Hashem God made earth and heaven” (Bereishis 2:4).

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 8b. Another baraisa teaches: “For it is a statute for Israel” (Tehillim 81:5). This tells me only about Israel. From where do we learn of the nations of the world? Scripture says, “A judgment for the God of Yaakov.” What, then, does “For it is a statute for Israel” teach? Israel enters for judgment first. This follows Rav Chisda. Rav Chisda said: Between the king and the public, the king enters for judgment first, as it says, “The judgment of His servant and the judgment of His people” (I Melachim 8:59). Why? If you wish, say that it is improper for a king to wait outside. If you wish, say that he enters before fierce anger increases.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 88a. A sectarian saw Rava studying the law. Rava’s fingers were beneath his leg, and he was pressing on them until they bled. The man said, “You rash people, who put your mouths before your ears, you still persist in your recklessness. You should first have listened. If you were able to fulfill it, you should have accepted it. If you were unable, you should not have accepted it.” Rava answered, “Of us, who proceed with wholeheartedness, Scripture says, ‘The wholeheartedness of the upright guides them.’ Of those people, who proceed with guile, it says, ‘The perversity of the treacherous destroys them’” (Mishlei 11:3).

paragraphs.text: Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 3:4. Although sounding the shofar on Rosh Hashanah is a decree of Scripture, it contains a hint. As if to say, “Awake, sleepers, from your sleep. Rise, slumberers, from your slumber. Search your deeds, return in teshuvah, and remember your Creator. You who forget the truth in the vanities of the times and spend all your years in folly and emptiness that can neither help nor save, look to your souls and improve your ways and deeds. Let each of you abandon his evil way and his thought that is not good.”

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah and Tosafos 16a. Why do they sound a tekiah and a teruah while seated, and sound a tekiah and a teruah while standing? In order to confuse the accuser. Tosafos explains “in order to confuse the accuser” in the name of the Aruch, which cites the Yerushalmi. It is written, “He will swallow up death forever” (Yeshayahu 25:8), and it is also written, “On that day a great shofar will be sounded” (27:13). When he hears the sound of the shofar the first time, he is somewhat alarmed. When he hears it a second time, he says, “Surely this is the shofar meant by ‘a great shofar will be sounded,’ and the time has come for me to be swallowed up.” He is confused and has no opportunity to press his accusations.

paragraphs.text: Chullin 89a. “It was not because you were more numerous than all the peoples that Hashem desired you” (Devarim 7:7). The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel, “I desire you because even when I bestow greatness on you, you make yourselves small before Me. I gave greatness to Avraham and he said, ‘I am dust and ashes.’ To Moshe and Aharon, and they said, ‘What are we?’ To David, and he said, ‘I am a worm, not a man.’ The idolaters are different. I gave greatness to Nimrod and he said, ‘Come, let us build ourselves a city.’ To Pharaoh, and he said, ‘Who is Hashem?’ To Sancheriv, and he said, ‘Who among all the gods of the lands,’ and so forth. To Nevuchadnetzar, and he said, ‘I shall ascend above the heights of the clouds.’ To Chiram, king of Tyre, and he said, ‘I sit in the seat of God in the heart of the seas.’”

paragraphs.text: Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 1:1–2. There are four new years. On the first of Nisan is the new year for kings and for festivals. On the first of Elul is the new year for the tithe of animals. Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say it is on the first of Tishrei. On the first of Tishrei is the new year for years, for Sabbatical and Jubilee years, for plantings, and for vegetables. There are four times when the world is judged. On Pesach, for grain. On Shavuos, for the fruits of the trees. On Rosh Hashanah, all who enter the world pass before Him like bnei maron, as it says, “He Who forms their hearts together, Who understands all their deeds” (Tehillim 33:15).

Mishnah: Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 1:1 — “ארבעה ראשי שנים הם. באחד בניסן ראש השנה למלכים ולרגלים. באחד באלול ראש השנה למעשר בהמה. רבי אלעזר ורבי שמעון אומרים, באחד …”. Meforshei HaMishnah: Bartenura on Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 1:1 — “ארבעה ראשי שנים הן. למלכים. מלכי ישראל מונין להם מניסן. שאם מלך מלך בשבט או באדר, משהגיע ניסן כלתה לו שנה ומתחילין …”. Midrash: Midrash Lekach Tov Exodus 12:2:5-9 — “… הוא לכם שאתם מונין ללבנה ואומות העולם מונין לחמה. הקטן מונה לקטן, והגדול מונה לגדול. וכשם שהחודש מתחדש. כך ישראל עתידין להתחדש. …”. paragraphs.text: Ramchal, Derekh Hashem IV:7 §6, describes the return of a season as renewing something of the light and effect originally granted in it. In IV:8 §3 he applies this to Purim, linking its recurring illumination to both deliverance and the renewed acceptance of Torah.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 105a. Shmuel gave the following example of a compelling reply. Ten people came and sat before the prophet, who told them to repent. They replied, “If a master sells his slave or a husband divorces his wife, does either retain any claim over the other?” The Holy One, blessed be He, told the prophet to answer them: “What is your mother’s bill of divorce with which I sent her away? Or to which of My creditors did I sell you? Behold, for your sins you were sold, and for your transgressions your mother was sent away” (Yeshayahu 50:1). This is what Reish Lakish said: What is meant by “David My servant” and “Nevuchadnetzar My servant” (Yirmiyahu 43:10)? It was manifest and known before Him Who spoke and the world came into being that Israel would make this argument. Therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, anticipated them by calling Nevuchadnetzar His servant. When a servant acquires property, to whom does the servant belong, and to whom does the property belong?

paragraphs.text: Bamidbar, Rosh Hashanah, and Tosafos 21:1 and 3a. The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel had come by way of Asarim. He fought Israel and took captives from them. What report did the king of Arad hear? He heard that Aharon had died and the clouds of glory had departed, and he thought that permission had been granted to fight Israel. This is what is meant by “All the congregation saw that Aharon had expired” (Bamidbar 20:29). Rabbi Abahu said, “Do not read ‘they saw,’ but ‘they were seen.’” Tosafos states that the Midrash identifies the attackers as Amalek. As the poet wrote in the liturgical poem for Parashas Zachor, “He changed clothing and language to become like the king of Arad.” The Gemara later records a teaching that Sichon, Arad, and Canaan are the same person. He was called Sichon because he resembled a foal in the wilderness, Canaan on account of the kingdom he ruled, and his name was Arad. Others say that he was called Arad because he resembled a wild ass in the wilderness, Canaan on account of his kingdom, and his name was Sichon.

paragraphs.text: Esther Rabbah Proem 10. Rabbi Berechyah opened with “Who has acted and accomplished, summoning the generations from the beginning,” and so forth (Yeshayahu 41:4). From the beginning of creation, the Holy One, blessed be He, prepared for each person what was appropriate to him. Adam was first of the created people, Kayin first of killers, Hevel first of those killed, Noach first of survivors, Avraham first of the circumcised, Yitzchak first of those bound for sacrifice, Yaakov first of the wholehearted, Yehudah first of the tribes, Yosef first of the pious, Aharon first of the priests, Moshe first of the prophets, Yehoshua first of conquerors, Osniel first of those who allotted land, Shmuel first of anointers, Shaul first of the anointed, David first of musicians, Shlomo first of builders, Nevuchadnetzar first of destroyers, Achashverosh first of sellers, and Haman first of buyers. When everyone saw this, they began to cry, “Woe!” Hence, “It was in the days of Achashverosh.”

paragraphs.text: Megillah 14a. To what can Achashverosh and Haman be compared? To two men. One had an earthen mound in his field, and the other had a ditch in his field. The owner of the ditch said, “If only someone would sell me that mound!” The owner of the mound said, “If only someone would sell me access to that ditch!” In time they met. The owner of the ditch said to the owner of the mound, “Sell me your mound.” The reply was, “Take it for nothing. I only wish you would!”

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Ra’aya Mehemna, Ki Seitzei, and Megillah III 275b–276a, with HaSulam; 15a. If you cast aspersions on Esther by saying she was defiled by Achashverosh, and that despite this she merited to be clothed in the holy spirit, which is Malchus, as written, “Esther clothed herself in royalty” (Esther 5:1), you are maligning Malchus. The Holy One, blessed be He, has said: “I am Hashem, that is My name. I will not give My glory to another or My praise to idols” (Yeshayahu 42:8). This is the Shechinah, called name, glory, and praise. The holy spirit is the Shechinah, which is the name in which Esther was clothed. How can you say that she was defiled by Achashverosh? The sages of the Mishnah said of the Matron, who is Malchus, “His sovereignty rules over all” (Tehillim 103:19). She rules even over the forces of impurity. So once Esther clothed herself with Malchus, in the meaning of “Esther clothed herself in royalty,” she exercised dominion over Achashverosh and his nation. Of them it says, “And to slay their enemies” (Esther 9:16). If you say, Heaven forbid, that Achashverosh secluded himself with her, even though they were in one house she did not seclude herself with him. The matter is like Yosef, of whom it says, “She set down his garment beside her” (Bereishis 39:16). It says beged, which is related to the treachery of “the treacherous acted treacherously” (Yeshayahu 24:16), rather than levush. It is the outermost part of him, to which the forces of impurity can attach. There is a great secret here. Thus Esther’s name implies concealment, as in “You are a hiding place for me” (Tehillim 32:7). The Shechinah concealed her from Achashverosh and provided a female spirit in her place, while Esther returned to Mordechai’s arms. Mordechai, who knew the explicit Name and the seventy languages, accomplished this with wisdom. Megillah states: On “which is not according to the law” (Esther 4:16), Rabbi Abba says, “It was not according to the law: before now, it was under duress. Now it is voluntary.” On “If I perish, I perish,” Esther means, “Just as I was lost from my father’s house, so will I be lost to you.” See also Rav Tzadok’s discussion in Poked Akarim §5, opening aval, and Machashavos Charutz §20, opening v’al ken.

The matter is like Yosef, of whom it says, “She set down his garment beside her” (Bereishis 39:16). It says beged, which is related to the treachery of “the treacherous acted treacherously” (Yeshayahu 24:16), rather than levush. It is the outermost part of him, to which the forces of impurity can attach. There is a great secret here. Thus Esther’s name implies concealment, as in “You are a hiding place for me” (Tehillim 32:7). The Shechinah concealed her from Achashverosh and provided a female spirit in her place, while Esther returned to Mordechai’s arms. Mordechai, who knew the explicit Name and the seventy languages, accomplished this with wisdom. Megillah states: On “which is not according to the law” (Esther 4:16), Rabbi Abba says, “It was not according to the law: before now, it was under duress. Now it is voluntary.” On “If I perish, I perish,” Esther means, “Just as I was lost from my father’s house, so will I be lost to you.” See also Rav Tzadok’s discussion in Poked Akarim §5, opening aval, and Machashavos Charutz §20, opening v’al ken.

paragraphs.text: Berachos and Megillah 8b and 13a. It was taught: Rabban Gamliel said, “I love the Persians for three things. They are modest in eating, modest in the privy, and modest in intimate matters.” On “I have commanded My consecrated ones” (Yeshayahu 13:3), Rav Yosef taught, “These are the Persians, consecrated and destined for Gehinnom.” On “In the evening she would come, and in the morning she would return” (Esther 2:14), Rabbi Yochanan said, “From that wicked man’s disgrace we learn one merit of his. He did not have relations by day.”

Meforshei HaShas: Chidushei Agadot on Megillah 10b:13-14 — “… אשר עליו היה השכינה שרויה כפרש"י שם ואמר יעלה הדס כו' דהיינו שתעלה לגדולה ולשם טוב ולא תהא קרויה עוד אסתר ע"ש …”. Meforshei HaYerushalmi: Korban HaEdah on Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:5 — “… ראשון שהיתה תחלת קריאתו שלא כדין: אבל. אם עיברו השנה לאחר י"ד שהיתה הקריאה מתחלה כדין: לא בדא. אינו כן ואין צריך …”. Midrash: Otzar Midrashim Midrashim on Megilat Esther Midrash on the Book of Esther:1-3 — “… הרשע ששרף בית המקדש, יעלה הדס זו אסתר הצדקת שנקראת הדסה, והיה לה' לשם זו מקרא מגילה, לאות עולם לא יכרת אלו …”. Meforshei HaMidrash: Etz Yosef on Esther Rabbah 10:10:1-2 — “… ברוש זה מרדכי הצדיק כו' ותחת הסרפד זו ושתי הרשעה כו' יעלה הדס זו אסתר הצדקת שנקראת הדסה. והיה לה' לשם אלו”. paragraphs.text: Chagigah 15b. How did Rabbi Meir learn Torah from the mouth of Acher? Did Rabbah bar bar Channah not say in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: What is the meaning of the verse, “For the lips of the priest shall preserve knowledge, and they shall seek Torah from his mouth, for he is an angel of Hashem of Hosts” (Malachi 2:7)? If the teacher resembles an angel of Hashem of Hosts, they should seek Torah from his mouth. Otherwise, they should not seek Torah from his mouth. Reish Lakish answered: Rabbi Meir found and interpreted the verse, “Incline your ear, hear the words of the wise, and set your heart to My knowledge” (Mishlei 22:17). It does not say “to their knowledge” but “to My knowledge.” The Gemara concludes, “Rabbi Meir found a pomegranate, ate its inside, and threw away its peel.”

paragraphs.text: Berachos 17a. Rav often said: The World to Come does not resemble this world. In the World to Come there is no eating or drinking, no procreation, no commerce, no jealousy, hatred, or rivalry. The righteous sit with crowns upon their heads and take pleasure in the radiance of the Shechinah.

Talmud Bavli: Megillah 2b — “… ישראל נינהו? ועוד: ״מהודו ועד כוש״ כתיב. ואימא: פרזים בארביסר מוקפין בארביסר ובחמיסר, כדכתיב: ״להיות עושים את יום ארבעה עשר לחדש אדר …”. Talmud Yerushalmi: Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:1 — “… המוקפין חומה מימות יהושע בן נון קורין בחמשה עשר. כפרים ועיירות גדולות קורין בארבעה עשר אלא שהכפרים מקדימין ליום הכניסה: הלכה: מגילה …”. Meforshei HaYerushalmi: Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:2 — “… מקדמינן: חל להיות ע"ש כפרים וכו' ועיירות גדולות ומוקפות חומה קורין בו ביום. שאין קריאת המגילה בשבת שגזרו חכמים שמא ילך אצל …”. Mishnah: Mishnah Megillah 1:1 — “… יותר. כרכין המקפין חומה מימות יהושע בן נון, קורין בחמשה עשר. כפרים ועירות גדולות, קורין בארבעה עשר, אלא שהכפרים מקדימין ליום הכניסה:”. paragraphs.text: Yerushalmi Peah 1:1. The Omnipresent joins a good intention to an action, but does not join an evil intention to an action. This is said regarding Israel. It is reversed for the nations: the Holy One, blessed be He, does not join a good intention to an action, but does join an evil intention to an action.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 64a. Rabbi Levi bar Chiya said: One who goes out of the synagogue and enters the study hall and engages in Torah merits greeting the Shechinah, as it says, “They go from strength to strength. Each appears before God in Zion” (Tehillim 84:8). Rabbi Chiya bar Ashi said in the name of Rav: Torah scholars have no rest in this world or the World to Come, as it says, “They go from strength to strength. Each appears before God in Zion.”

paragraphs.text: Niddah 16b. Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa expounded: The angel placed in charge of conception is named Lailah. He takes the drop and presents it before the Holy One, blessed be He. He asks, “Master of the world, what shall become of this drop? Will the person be strong or weak, wise or foolish, rich or poor?” But he does not say “wicked or righteous,” in keeping with Rabbi Chanina’s teaching. Rabbi Chanina said, “Everything is in the hands of Heaven except fear of Heaven,” as it says, “And now, Israel, what does Hashem your God ask of you but to fear,” and so forth (Devarim 10:12).

paragraphs.text: Bava Basra 16a. Rava said: Iyov sought to exempt the whole world from judgment. He said before God, “Master of the world, You created the ox with split hooves and the donkey with unbroken hooves. You created Gan Eden and Gehinnom. You created righteous people and wicked people. Who can restrain You?” What did Iyov’s friends answer him? “You even annul fear and diminish prayer before God” (Iyov 15:4). The Holy One, blessed be He, created the evil inclination and created Torah as its seasoning.

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 65a. “אתון איכא עלייכו אימתא דמלכותא אנן לא תיהוי עלן אימתא דמלכותא” Rava found Bar Sheshach immersed up to his neck in rosewater, with unclothed prostitutes standing before him. Bar Sheshach asked, “Will you have anything like this in the World to Come?” Rava said, “Ours will be better than this.” Bar Sheshach asked what could be better. Rava replied, “You are subject to fear of the government. We will have no fear of the government upon us.” Bar Sheshach said that he himself had no fear of the government. While they sat there, the king’s messenger came and told him to get up because the king wanted him. As he was leaving, he said to Rava, “May the eye that wishes to see evil befall you burst.” Rava answered, “Amen,” and Bar Sheshach’s eye burst.

paragraphs.text: Ta’anis 26b. “לא היו ימים טובים לישראל כחמשה עשר באב וכיום הכפורים” Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said that Israel had no holidays like the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur. The daughters of Jerusalem would go out and dance in the vineyards. They would say, “Young man, lift your eyes and see whom you would choose. Set your eyes upon family rather than beauty. ‘Grace is false and beauty is fleeting. A woman who fears Hashem is to be praised.’ It also says, ‘Give her of the fruit of her hands, and let her deeds praise her in the gates.’”

paragraphs.text: Yoma 19b–20a. “שטן ביומא דכיפורי לית ליה רשותא לאסטוני” Distinguished people of Jerusalem stayed awake all night so the high priest would hear the sound of the crowd and would not be overcome by sleep. Abba Shaul taught that they did the same outside the Temple in memory of it, but this led to sin. Rashi explains that men and women would amuse themselves together and come to transgression. Abaye, or Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak, identifies Nehardea in particular. Eliyahu said to Rav Yehudah, the brother of Rav Sala Chasida, “You ask why Mashiach has not come. Today is Yom Kippur, yet how many maidens had relations in Nehardea!” He asked, “What did the Holy One, blessed be He, say?” Eliyahu answered, “‘Sin crouches at the door.’” He further asked, “What did the Accuser say?” Eliyahu answered, “On Yom Kippur he has no permission to accuse.” Rami bar Chama derives this from the numerical value of ha-satan, 364. On 364 days he has permission to accuse, while on Yom Kippur he has none.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 118a. “כל המענג את השבת נותנין לו נחלה בלי מצרים” Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yose, “Whoever delights in Shabbos is granted an inheritance without boundaries.” As Scripture says, “If you restrain your foot on account of Shabbos from pursuing your affairs on My holy day, call Shabbos a delight and Hashem’s holy day honored, and honor it by refraining from pursuing your ways or attending to your affairs or speaking of them, then you will delight in Hashem. I will cause you to ride upon the heights of the earth and feed you with the inheritance of your father Yaakov.” It is neither the inheritance promised to Avraham, “Arise, walk through the land, its length and its breadth,” nor the one promised to Yitzchak, “To you and your descendants I will give all these lands.” It is the inheritance of Yaakov, “You will spread westward, eastward, northward, and southward.” The printed text cites 118b.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 31b. “מי שאכל שום וריחו נודף יחזור ויאכל שום אחר ויהא ריחו נודף” Rav Ulla expounded, “Do not be excessively wicked.” Does that mean one should avoid only a great deal of wickedness and may be a little wicked? The meaning is that one who has eaten garlic and already smells of it should ask himself whether he ought to eat more garlic and smell even more. Rashi explains that the verse tells a person who has done a little wickedness to refrain from adding to it, just as eating more garlic only prolongs the odor noticeable to others.

paragraphs.text: Shemos Rabbah 29:4. “שני דברים שאלו ישראל מלפני הקב״ה שיראו כבודו וישמעו קולו” Rabbi Levi said that Israel asked two things of the Holy One, blessed be He, to see His glory and to hear His voice. They saw His glory and heard His voice, as it says, “Hashem our God has shown us His glory and greatness,” and “We heard His voice from the midst of the fire.” They could not withstand it. When they came to Sinai and He appeared and spoke to them, their souls departed, as it says, “My soul went out when He spoke.” Torah pleaded for mercy before the Holy One, blessed be He, “Does a king marry off his daughter and kill the members of his own household? Is the whole world rejoicing while Your children die?” Their souls immediately returned, as it says, “The Torah of Hashem is perfect, restoring the soul.”

paragraphs.text: Berachos 8a. “קשה שבכולן אסכרא ניחא שבכולן נשיקה” It was taught that 903 kinds of death were created in the world, as it says, “The ways out belong to death.” The word totza’os has that numerical value. The hardest is askara, a choking affliction, and the gentlest is death by a kiss. Askara is like thorn branches pulled backward out of tangled wool. Rashi says some wool inevitably tears away with them. Another account compares it to thick ropes forced through tight holes to join the planks of a ship in seas where iron does not hold. Death by a kiss is like drawing a hair out of milk.

paragraphs.text: Pirkei Avos 5:6. “עשרה דברים נבראו בערב שבת בין השמשות” Ten things were created at twilight on the eve of Shabbos. paragraphs.text: In Gittin 60a, Rashi explains that the weakening of memory and the risk of Torah being forgotten made it necessary to write teachings down. Temurah 14b cites R. Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish studying a written collection of aggadah. These are concrete instances of Rav Tzadok’s principle that suspending a rule of transmission can preserve the Torah itself.

paragraphs.text: Megillah 7a. “שלחה להם אסתר לחכמים קבעוני לדורות ... כתבוני לדורות” Rav Shmuel bar Yehudah said that Esther sent to the sages, “Establish me for all generations.” They replied, “You are arousing hostility against us among the nations.” She replied, “I am already recorded in the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia.” Rav, Rav Chanina, Rabbi Yonasan, and Rav Chaviva taught that she sent, “Write me for all generations.” The sages replied, “Have I not written for you in threes?” They understood that as three accounts and no fourth. Then they found it written in the Torah, “Write this as a memorial in the book.” “Write this” refers to what is written here and in Devarim, “as a memorial” to what is written in the Prophets, and “in the book” to what is written in the Megillah.

paragraphs.text: Megillah 11a. “אימתי ראו כל אפסי ארץ את ישועת אלהינו בימי מרדכי ואסתר” Rabbi Yochanan opened his exposition of this account with “He remembered His kindness and faithfulness to the house of Israel. All the ends of the earth saw the salvation of our God.” When did all the ends of the earth see the salvation of our God? In the days of Mordechai and Esther.

paragraphs.text: Menachos 85b. “תקוע אלפא לשמן ... מתוך שרגילין בשמן זית חכמה מצויה בה” The Mishnah calls Tekoa first among places producing oil. Its oil stands at the head of all other oils just as alef stands at the head of the letters. The Gemara cites “Yoav sent to Tekoa and took a wise woman from there.” Why Tekoa? Rabbi Yochanan explains that since its residents regularly use olive oil, wisdom is found there.

paragraphs.text: II Chronicles 20:35–37. “כהתחברך עם אחזיהו פרץ ה׳ את מעשיך וישברו אניות” Afterward, Yehoshafat king of Yehudah joined Achazyah king of Israel, who acted wickedly. He joined him in building ships to travel to Tarshish. They built the ships in Etzyon Gever. Eliezer son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied concerning Yehoshafat, “Because you joined Achazyah, Hashem has broken up what you have made.” The ships were wrecked and could not sail to Tarshish.

paragraphs.text: Tosafos on Sotah 35b, citing Yerushalmi Sotah 7:5. “שלושה מיני אבנים הן ... באבנים שהקים יהושע להן על גב הירדן” The Yerushalmi distinguishes three sets of stones, the stones of the encampment, the stones Yehoshua put under the feet of the priests, and the stelae Moshe gave to Israel. Korban HaEdah explains that Moshe expounded the Torah, “Moshe undertook to explain this Torah,” and this too was on stones. Rabbi Yitzchak took it as plain that there were four sets. Rabbi Simon bar Zevida concurred. Scripture says of the fourth set, “These stones shall be a memorial to the children of Israel forever.” The encampment stones were temporary and were hidden. The stones Yehoshua placed under the feet of the priests are submerged. The stelae Moshe gave them had already entered the Land with them. Thus the verse refers to the stones Yehoshua erected on the banks of the Jordan.

paragraphs.text: Bava Basra 3b. “כל מאן דאתי ואמר מבית חשמונאי קאתינא עבדא הוא” Herod was a slave of the Hasmonean house. He set his eyes on a young woman of that family. One day he heard a heavenly voice say that any slave who rebelled at that time would succeed. He arose and killed his masters, sparing only that young woman. Seeing that he meant to marry her, she went up to the roof and cried out, “Whoever comes and says, ‘I descend from the Hasmonean house,’ is a slave. The only one left of that house is this young woman.” She then fell from the roof to the ground.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 22a. “מים אין בו אבל נחשים ועקרבים יש בו” Rav Kahana said that Rav Nasan bar Manyumi taught in Rabbi Tanchum’s name that a Chanukah lamp placed higher than twenty cubits is invalid, like a sukkah or the crossbeam at the entrance to an alley. Rav Kahana also transmitted the following in the same names. Scripture says, “The pit was empty. There was no water in it.” If it says the pit was empty, why say there was no water in it? There was no water, but there were snakes and scorpions.

paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 122a describes Elazar announcing a tribe and its territory through the Urim and Tummim before the two lots were drawn. Rashbam explains that the agreement between the prior announcement and the lot reassured Israel that the division was just. This shows why Rav Tzadok adduces that lot as an instance of reliable disclosure.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III, Vayikra 7a, HaSulam. “ומתי נקרא האדם שלם כעין של מעלה” When is a person called complete in the likeness of what is above? When he joins his wife in unity, joy, and willingness, and they have a son and a daughter. He is then complete in the likeness of what is above, bringing completeness below in the likeness of the Holy Name above. Yud and heh are the mystery of father and mother. Vav and heh are the mystery of son and daughter. The supernal Holy Name is then called upon him.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 156a. “צא מאיצטגנינות שלך שאין מזל לישראל” Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name, “From where do we know that Israel is not bound by the stars? Scripture says, ‘He brought him outside.’” Avraham said to the Holy One, blessed be He, “Master of the world, a member of my household is to inherit me.” God answered, “No. One who issues from your own body will be your heir.” He said, “I have looked at my astrological reckoning, and I am not fit to have a son.” God answered, “Leave your astrological reckoning, for Israel is not bound by the stars.”

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 17a. “אין הדבר תלוי אלא בי ... רבי אלעזר בן דורדיא מזומן לחיי העולם הבא” It was taught of Rabbi Elazar ben Dordaya that he did not leave a single prostitute in the world without going to her. On one occasion he heard of a prostitute in a coastal city who charged a purse of dinars. He took a purse of dinars and crossed seven rivers to reach her. During the act she passed wind and said, “Just as this wind will never return to where it came from, so Elazar ben Dordaya will never be accepted in repentance.” He sat between two mountains and hills and asked them to plead for mercy on his behalf. They said, “Before we plead for you, let us plead for ourselves,” since Scripture says, “The mountains will move and the hills will totter.” He asked heaven and earth to plead for him. They gave the same answer, citing “The heavens will vanish like smoke and the earth will wear out like a garment.” He asked the sun and moon, and they likewise answered with “The moon will be abashed and the sun ashamed.” He asked the stars and constellations, and they answered with “All the host of heaven will melt away.” He said, “It depends upon me alone.” He put his head between his knees and cried aloud until his soul left him. A heavenly voice came forth and announced, “Rabbi Elazar ben Dordaya is destined for life in the World to Come.”

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 65:22. “וירח את ריח בגדיו ויברכהו כגון יוסף משיתא ויקום איש צרורות” “He smelled the scent of his garments and blessed him.” The Midrash gives Yosef Meshisa and Yakum Ish Tzeroros as examples. When enemies wanted to enter the Temple Mount, they said someone from among the Jews should enter first. They told Yosef Meshisa to enter and keep whatever he brought out. He entered and brought out a golden Menorah. They told him that an ordinary man should not use such a thing and told him to enter again and keep what he brought out next. He refused. Rabbi Pinchas says that they offered him the tax revenue for three years, but he refused. He said, “Was it not enough that I angered my God once, that I should anger Him a second time?” They put him on a carpenter’s horse and sawed into him. He cried aloud, “Alas that I angered my Creator!” Yakum Ish Tzeroros was a nephew of Rabbi Yose ben Yoezer of Tzereidah. He rode a horse on Shabbos as his uncle was taken out to be hanged on a beam. He told his uncle, “See the horse on which my master has mounted me and the horse on which your Master has mounted you.” Rabbi Yose replied, “If that is the reward accorded to those who anger Him, how much more to those who do His will!” His nephew asked if anyone had done God’s will more than Rabbi Yose. He replied, “If that is what befalls those who do His will, how much more those who anger Him!” The words entered Yakum like a serpent’s venom. He then inflicted upon himself the four judicial deaths, stoning, burning, beheading, and strangling. Rabbi Yose ben Yoezer dozed and saw his nephew’s bier rising through the air. He said, “In a single moment this one preceded me to Gan Eden.”

paragraphs.text: Menachos 44a. “אותן מצעות שהציעה לו באיסור הציעה לו בהיתר” A man who was scrupulous about tzitzis heard of a prostitute in a coastal city who charged four hundred gold coins. He sent her the coins and arranged a time. He came at the appointed time and sat at the entrance. Her maid informed her that the man who paid four hundred gold coins had arrived. She told her to admit him. She prepared seven beds, six of silver and one of gold, with silver ladders between them and a golden ladder at the top. She went up and sat unclothed on the top bed, and he began to ascend unclothed to sit facing her. His four fringes slapped him in the face, and he slipped down and sat on the ground. She did the same and told him, “By the goddess of Rome, I will not let you go until you tell me what blemish you saw in me.” He swore that he had never seen anyone as beautiful, but Hashem had given one commandment called tzitzis that says “I am Hashem your God” twice. He understood this as “I will exact punishment, and I will pay reward.” His fringes had appeared to him like four witnesses. She asked his name, his town, his teacher, and the study hall where he learned Torah. He wrote them and gave the note to her. She divided her possessions, giving a third to the government and a third to the poor, keeping a third as well as the bedding. She came to Rabbi Chiya’s study hall and asked to be made a convert. He asked if she had set her eyes on a disciple. She handed him the note, and he told her, “Go, take what you have acquired.” The same bedding she had set out for him in prohibition she now set out for him in permission. That was his reward in this world. The reward in the World to Come is beyond what I can know.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 63:13. “רבי שמואל בר נחמן אמר זה דם בכורה וקרבנות רבי לוי אמר זה דם של מילה” “I will make you blood, and blood will pursue you. Since you hated blood, blood will pursue you.” Esav hates blood. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman said that this is the blood of the birthright and the offerings. Rabbi Levi said it is the blood of circumcision.

paragraphs.text: Yevamos 63a. “אפילו ספינות הבאות מגליא לאספמיא אינן מתברכות אלא בשביל ישראל” Rabbi Elazar interpreted “All the families of the earth shall be blessed through you.” The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Avraham, “I have two good plantings to graft upon you, Rus the Moabite and Naamah the Ammonite.” Even families living in the earth are blessed only on Israel’s account. “All the nations of the earth” includes even the ships from Galia to Aspamia, which are blessed only on Israel’s account.

paragraphs.text: Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 244, and Shemos 14:20. “ראתה שפחה על הים מה שלא ראה יחזקאל וישעיה” Rabbi Eliezer interprets “This is my God.” How do we know that a maidservant at the sea saw what Yechezkel and Yeshayahu did not see? Scripture says, “Through the prophets I used likenesses,” and “The heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.” It is like a human king entering a province, surrounded by his company, with warriors to his right and left and troops in front and behind. Everyone asks which man is the king, as he is mortal like them. When the Holy One, blessed be He, appeared at the sea, no one needed to ask who the King was. They recognized Him as soon as they saw Him and all exclaimed, “This is my God and I will glorify Him.” “It came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel. There were cloud and darkness, and it illuminated the night. One did not approach the other throughout the night.”

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 49:2 and 47:9. “וכרות עמו מלמד שהיה הקב״ה אוחז בו ... בדק את עצמו ומצא עצמו מהול” Avraham said before Him, “Who will circumcise me?” The Holy One, blessed be He, answered, “You yourself.” Avraham immediately took a knife, held his foreskin, and started to cut, but he was afraid because he was old. The Holy One, blessed be He, extended His hand and held it together with him, and Avraham cut. Scripture says, “You are Hashem, the God Who chose Avram,” and continues, “You cut the covenant with him.” It says “with him” rather than “for him,” teaching that the Holy One, blessed be He, held it with him. Rabbi Levi makes a second inference. Scripture says that Avraham “was circumcised” rather than that he circumcised himself. He examined himself and found himself circumcised.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 93a and 106a. “אלוהיהם של אלו שונא זימה הוא” In the account involving Nevuchadnetzar, Achav and Tzidkiyahu tried to seduce his daughter, claiming that they had received a prophecy from Hashem. When she told her father, he knew they were lying, because “the God of these people hates sexual immorality.” He tested them in a fiery furnace and they burned. In the account of Bilaam, after failing to curse Israel, he advised Balak to entice them to sexual immorality, for “the God of these people hates sexual immorality.”

paragraphs.text: Megillah 12a. “הם לא עשו אלא לפנים ... כי לא ענה מלבו” Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai’s students asked why the Jews of that generation were liable to annihilation. He told them to give their own answer. They said it was because they enjoyed the feast of that wicked man. He replied that in that case only the people in Shushan should have been killed, with the rest of the world spared. They asked for his own answer. He said it was because they bowed down to the image. They asked whether He showed them favoritism. He answered, “They acted only outwardly, and the Holy One, blessed be He, acted toward them only outwardly.” This is the meaning of “He did not afflict them from His heart.”

Machshavah: Notes by Rabbi Yehoshua Hartman on Ohr Chadash 5:12:35-40 — “צרף לכאן שעשו זקנו של המן אמר בראשית לג ט יש לי רב בעוד שיעקב אבינו אמר שם פסוק יא יש לי …”. Rav Tzadok elsewhere (HaMafteach HaShalem): Peri Tzadik, Miketz 6 — “… התיקון שיהיה אכילתו בקדושה ועי"ז זוכה לכל הקדושות וכמ"ש (תענית יא.) לעולם ימוד אדם עצמו כאלו קדוש שרוי בתוך מעיו …”; Resisei Layla 58; Takanat HaShavin 6 — “… גם בבני ישראל ועל כן הסכים לו השם יתברך, ומכל מקום נקרא שהוא ייתר הפרשה בתורה כי אין זה מצד …”.

Meforshei HaYerushalmi: Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 8:1 — “… השבוע ושבת עצמו בכלל איסור של שבוע שעברה דכי אמר שבת זו דעתייהו על ימי החול הבאים ועל יום השבת: חדש זה. …”. Mishnah: Mishnah Oktzin 3:12 — “… אמלא. אמר רבי שמעון בן חלפתא, לא מצא הקדוש ברוך הוא כלי מחזיק ברכה לישראל אלא השלום, שנאמר (תהלים כט), ה' עז …”. Meforshei HaMishnah: Rambam on Mishnah Megillah 3:4 — “… להיות בשבת קורין בפרשת שקלים כו': שבת ראשונה היא שבכלל ימותיה היא ראש חדש אדר והוא כשיתחיל ראש חדש אדר יום ראשון …”. Midrash: Bamidbar Rabbah 21:1 — “… הוא שיטל שכרו, (במדבר כה, יב) : לכן אמר הנני נתן לו את בריתי שלום, גדול השלום שנתן לפנחס, שאין העולם מתנהג …”. Meforshei HaMidrash: Perush Maharzu on Vayikra Rabbah 9:9:1-2 — “… ופרשה י"ב סימן ח' וסוף פרשה י"ט וד"ר פרשה ה' סי' י"ב: שכל הברכות כלולות בו. שהשלום כלי מחזיק ברכה וזהו מ"ש …”. Rav Tzadok elsewhere (HaMafteach HaShalem): Yisrael Kedoshim 10 — “… אמרו שכולם יש להם חלק לעולם הבא מצד אור הרשימו מיהת ומצד הזה גם כן אי אפשר לעקור שם ישראל …”; Resisei Layla 58; Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Eruvin 3 — “… ז' וזהו גם כן ענין שמיטין ויובלות ואין כאן מקום להאריך עוד. וכן כאן שיהיה בעליל לארץ צריך שלשים פעמים …”.
